title: The Caro-Kann Defense
description: A reliable, low-risk defense to 1.e4. Black supports a future d5 with c6, avoiding the cramped bishop of the French while keeping a sturdy structure.

sections.title: Why c6?
sections.content: After 1.e4 c6, Black prepares d5 with pawn support. Unlike the French, the light-squared bishop can develop actively to f5 or g4 before being locked in.

positions.commentary: The Caro-Kann. Black will follow with d5, challenging the center while keeping the c8 bishop's diagonal open.

sections.title: The Active Bishop
sections.content: A hallmark of the Caro-Kann is developing the light-squared bishop to f5 before playing e6. This solves the classic problem bishop of 1.e4 e6 setups.

positions.commentary: Black has developed the bishop to f5 outside the pawn chain — a key strategic achievement of the Caro-Kann.

exercises.title: Challenge the Center
exercises.description: White to play. Develop a knight to attack the d5 pawn.
hints: Add a defender of e4 and attacker of d5
